declared_purpose: ClawDefender screens untrusted input for security threats, scans skills and workspace scripts, checks URLs before fetching, and installs then scans ClawHub skills. Sanitization explicitly supports content passthrough, warnings, reports and strict blocking. These purposes are documented in SKILL.md, lines 3–8, 40–81 and 83–126.

data_operations.operation: Read text locally, infer threat categories and return a security assessment.
data_operations.data_scope: Entire supplied text or command; four pattern modules produce categories, severity, score and action. Human output contains pattern definitions rather than matched input values; JSON contains summary attributes. Supplied commands are not executed.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local shell and validation subprocesses; stdout to the caller.
data_operations.condition: --check-prompt reads stdin; --check-command and --validate read arguments. These checks implement the declared screening purpose.

data_operations.operation: Inspect a URL locally and infer a safe or dangerous classification.
data_operations.data_scope: Entire URL, checked against substring domain allowances and SSRF patterns. This execution path does not run the credential-exfiltration validator or fetch the URL.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local validation processes; classification and matching pattern definitions returned to the caller.
data_operations.condition: --check-url; an allowed-domain substring bypasses the SSRF pattern checks.

data_operations.operation: Read external content and pass it to the local scanner.
data_operations.source: sanitize.sh argument or stdin, potentially containing email, API responses or other external content.
data_operations.data_scope: Entire input, retained in INPUT and forwarded through stdin to clawdefender.sh. --json sets MODE but does not select JSON parsing or string-field extraction in the supplied implementation.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local sanitizer memory and the local clawdefender.sh child process; scanner output is captured in RESULT.
data_operations.condition: Every sanitizer invocation with input, including --json. Reading content is necessary for screening; whole-text JSON checking is an implementation choice.

data_operations.operation: Return original content or a detection report; conditionally suppress content.
data_operations.source: Sanitizer INPUT and captured scanner RESULT.
data_operations.data_scope: Default output includes the original content, wrapped when CRITICAL or WARNING is recognized. Warnings include severity and up to three pattern definitions. Report mode returns detection information without original content; strict mode suppresses content on recognized detections.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Stdout and stderr to the caller; no additional storage or remote recipient is specified.
data_operations.condition: --report takes precedence over --strict. --silent suppresses stderr warnings but still returns content. HIGH-only findings do not satisfy the sanitizer's detection condition and therefore pass through, including in strict mode. Passthrough itself is explicitly documented.

data_operations.operation: Read skill and script files locally, classify their contents and return findings.
data_operations.source: /home/clawdbot/clawd/skills and /home/clawdbot/clawd/scripts, or the skill path derived from a supplied name.
data_operations.data_scope: Full contents of skill files ending in .md, .sh, .js, .py or .ts, excluding paths containing node_modules, .git or .min.js. Full audits also read workspace .sh scripts with specified exclusions. Output includes skill names, flagged basenames, pattern definitions and counts, rather than raw file contents.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local validation processes and the caller's stdout.
data_operations.condition: --scan-skill, --audit, or the post-install scan. Full audits skip security-scanner, clawdefender and proactive-agent skills, plus two named scanner scripts.

data_operations.operation: Inspect sensitive-file metadata and infer a permission warning.
data_operations.data_scope: File existence and numeric permission bits, not credential contents.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local stat process and permission assessment returned to the caller.
data_operations.condition: --audit, when the .env file exists. This is a supporting workspace security check.

data_operations.operation: Append audit history to a local file.
data_operations.source: Audit execution time and aggregate scan results.
data_operations.data_scope: Timestamp, finding count and inferred Clean or Review needed status; no raw scanned content or credential values.
data_operations.condition: Every --audit execution attempts append writes. Persistence is an implementation choice; the entry document requires scanning and reporting but does not require audit-history retention.

data_operations.operation: Delegate skill installation to an external component and return its output.
data_operations.data_scope: Skill identifier passed to npx clawhub install with --no-input; working directory is /home/clawdbot/clawd. Installer stdout and stderr reach the caller. Subsequent code expects an installed directory under skills.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local npx/clawhub process; its remote recipients, additional reads and persistence are unspecified by the supplied source.
data_operations.condition: --install. Running npx clawhub install and subsequently scanning are explicitly documented requirements; installer internals remain unresolved.

data_operations.operation: Recursively delete the directory selected for an installed skill.
data_operations.data_scope: All files beneath the derived directory, not merely flagged files. The wrapper does not constrain or canonicalize the supplied skill name.
data_operations.condition: Installation succeeds, the directory exists, scanning reports findings, and the keep response is not Y or y. This conditional removal is an implementation choice beyond the documented warning requirement.

data_operations.operation: Read and return whitelist configuration; echo an attempted addition without storing it.
data_operations.data_scope: Entire existing whitelist JSON for list; supplied pattern for add. Actual whitelist contents are not supplied.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local cat/jq processes and stdout to the caller. The add branch performs no JSON update.
data_operations.condition: --whitelist list reads the file; --whitelist add echoes the pattern and reports that implementation is absent.

data_operations.operation: Document external-content retrieval followed by local sanitization.
data_operations.source: Example API endpoints and caller-provided email, API and GitHub retrieval commands.
data_operations.data_scope: Retrieved external content is piped into sanitize.sh. Example curl requests target the supplied API URL; the scanner does not itself initiate these retrievals.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Retrieval service selected by the example or caller, then the local sanitizer and its caller.
data_operations.condition: Only when users adopt the examples or heartbeat integration. The examples do not establish a remote disclosure of scanned workspace files.

data_operations.operation: Require or illustrate user notification after detection.
data_operations.source: Detection results or filtered audit output.
data_operations.data_scope: Alert content is unspecified; the cron example filters CRITICAL or HIGH lines and conditionally invokes notify_user without explicit arguments.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: The user as the documented recipient; notification transport and any persistence are unspecified.
data_operations.condition: Documentation instructs alerting on flagged content and illustrates a cron notification. The packaged scripts emit local output but contain no notification implementation.

potential_excess.data_scope: Accumulating audit timestamps, finding counts and inferred security status.
potential_excess.condition: Each --audit execution appends a record; no retention limit or cleanup is implemented in the supplied source.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The declared audit outcome is scanning installed skills and scripts and showing findings. Persistent history is not explicitly required.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Read the selected files, perform local checks and return the current assessment to the caller.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Make history logging optional. If history is wanted, bound retention or overwrite a latest-result record. This removes optional persistence rather than reducing data needed for scanning.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep current scan coverage and caller-visible findings. Retain bounded history only when an actual history requirement exists.

unknowns: Installer disclosure and persistence assessment is blocked by absent npx/clawhub source: remote endpoints, transmitted data, additional filesystem reads, caches and cleanup cannot be established.

The installer’s handling of skill identifiers is unknown. Although the wrapper leaves the derived scan/deletion path unconstrained, whether an identifier selecting an unrelated directory can reach that branch depends on installer success and runtime state.
Caller handling of returned content, whitelist JSON and detection output is not supplied. Subsequent forwarding or retention cannot be attributed to this skill.
notify_user and other retrieval/notification commands are not supplied; their alert payloads, recipients beyond the intended user, and retention remain unresolved.
Runtime audit-log access controls, external retention policies and actual whitelist contents are not supplied.
